conditions.note: a measurement on this machine under this load. Not a capacity plan: a single-process figure extrapolated to an estate is arithmetic rather than evidence
conditions.shared_machine: other agent sessions were running on this machine throughout, and this session left orphaned processes of its own. That is the most likely explanation for two runs in which a read that takes 33 s did not return in half an hour, and it is a reason to trust the DIRECT measurements in `docs/10 §2.4a` over anything this spike reports about the heavy reads

detail: measured at 10000, 50000 models. 6 of 6 target comparisons met. The figure to read is the SLOPE rather than either number: a read whose cost grows with the estate is one that works until it does not, and no amount of headroom at today's size tells you where that is
not_measured: the write path. The estate is seeded as rows, so registration, the approval quorum and the serialised evidence append are not timed here at any size

evidence chain verification at estate size. The seeded register has no chain; 6,000 nodes in `tests/test_scale.py` is the largest this repository has observed, and `NFR-PERF-005` is asking about 50,000 models' worth
concurrency. One process, one request at a time — a p95 under load is a different number and this is the floor under it
PostgreSQL. Measured on SQLite, where the whole estate is one file on local disk. A network round trip per query moves every figure here
anything multi-node: failover, replica reads, RTO and RPO (`NFR-AVAIL-001`, `NFR-AVAIL-003`) are untouched by this

reads_not_taken.dashboard: not taken by this spike. Measured separately: 1,714 ms at 2,000 models, which is the same fold as `/portfolio` — the dashboard assembles the worklist across the estate. Session authentication is NOT the cost: `/models` is 12 ms under a session against 24 ms under HTTP Basic
reads_not_taken.portfolio: 8,258 ms p95 over 7 samples at 10,000 models in this spike. Measured directly afterwards, the fold was 33.4 s at 50,000 and LINEAR at 0.67 ms per model — the spike's failure to return at that size was an artefact of a shared machine, not a property of the fold, and an earlier version of this file said otherwise. The fold is now 7.6 s at 50,000; see `docs/10 §2.4a`. These figures predate that fix
